articles.titulo: Development of a model of tick-borne encephalitis virus transmission from experimentally infected bank voles to Ixodes ricinus ticks
articles.autores: Sick F, Răileanu C, … Wernike K (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is an important arbovirus in Europe. TBEV is transmitted mainly by ticks of the Ixodes ricinus (Ixodes ricinus-Ixodes persulcatus) species complex and causes infections of the central nervous system, making it one of the most important viral tick-borne diseases of humans in Europe. The natural transmission cycle relies on a complex interplay of arthropod vector and mammalian host factors. Besides the infection of ticks by feeding on viremic animals and co-feeding, transstadial transmission of the virus within the tick is also essential for further TBEV transmission to the next vertebrate host during the subsequent bloodmeal. In this study, we attempted to establish a mammalian host-tick transmission model for the simulation of the natural transmission under controlled laboratory conditions in order to study virus transmission from the reservoir host bank vole (Myodes glareolus) to I. ricinus larvae and to evaluate transstadial transmission of TBEV when engorged larvae moult into nymphs. We demonstrated acquisition of TBEV by larval ticks that blood fed on TBEV-infected viremic bank voles, although the TBEV infection prevalence of the engorged larvae was low (9.3%). Fully and partially engorged larvae were collected and further kept in the insectary and were allowed to moult into nymphs to assess transstadial virus transmission. No transstadial virus transmission was observed, as all nymphs tested negative by real-time RT-PCR. Although no general conclusions on transstadial transmission could be drawn yet, the establishment of this model forms a basis for future research.

articles.titulo: The effects of environmental temperature on the extrinsic incubation period of arboviruses in their mosquito vectors: A systematic review
articles.autores: Hartner AM, Herath T, … Irrgang C (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Arboviruses are an increasing global public health concern, driven by both human and environmental factors. A key parameter shaping vectorial capacity for transmission is the extrinsic incubation period (EIP), the time required for a mosquito that has ingested an infectious blood meal to become capable of transmitting the virus via its saliva, which is strongly influenced by temperature. However, the temperature-EIP relationship remains poorly characterized across arboviruses and mosquito species.
We conducted the first systematic review of laboratory studies evaluating temperature effects on EIP across all reported mosquito-arbovirus pairings identifiable in the literature. We searched three databases and extracted data on infection and transmission efficiency (TE), applying a binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model to estimate the median extrinsic incubation period, the time post-infection at which 50% of infected mosquitoes become infectious.
Our synthesis included 53 studies covering 17 arboviruses. We found substantial heterogeneity in temperature effects on TE. Zika and West Nile viruses generally showed increased TE and shorter EIP at higher temperatures. However, similar trends based on published data were not clear for many viruses, such as Sindbis and chikungunya viruses, because of limited data granularity and small sample sizes. Even across different vectors of the same virus, findings varied widely, reflecting both biological differences and inconsistent experimental designs.
The findings revealed gaps in the understanding of the temperature effects on the EIP of arboviruses in mosquito vectors. Standardisation of reporting in vector competence experiments and expanded research on neglected viruses are urgently needed. Real-world environmental conditions should also be incorporated to improve modelling and support robust vector control and public health planning under changing climatic conditions.

v6.implicacao: Competência vetorial × estado metabólico (Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo) e comparação de competência de Aedes aegypti nos recortes do Rio (Epidemiologia de Precisão): o desenho deve registrar temperatura e reportar infecção, disseminação e transmissão por dia pós-infecção, a padronização que a revisão pede.
v6.resumo: Primeira revisão sistemática de estudos de laboratório sobre temperatura e período de incubação extrínseco (EIP): 53 estudos, 17 arbovírus. Zika e vírus do Nilo Ocidental mostram maior eficiência de transmissão e EIP mais curto em temperaturas altas; para Sindbis e chikungunya não há tendência clara, por dados escassos, e vetores do mesmo vírus divergem muito, em parte por desenhos experimentais inconsistentes.

articles.titulo: NF-κB/Dif-driven miR-1000 feedback restrains toll signaling via targeting Myd88 to restore Drosophila immune homeostasis
articles.autores: Jia C, Li J, … Jin P (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Innate immune homeostasis is vital for animal survival and requires precise control of both the intensity and duration of immune signaling. Although microRNAs (miRNAs) are known to fine-tune immune responses, their transcriptional regulation mechanisms during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify an NF-κB-dependent miRNA feedback loop essential for Drosophila Toll pathway. Through dynamic expression profiling and functional genetics, we demonstrate that the NF-κB transcription factor Dif directly activates miR-1000 transcription upon Gram-positive bacterial infection, while miR-1000 in turn targets the adaptor Myd88 mRNA for degradation. Moreover, we show that upon immune challenge, miR-1000 is significantly induced in the fat body, and fat body-specific manipulations confirm that Dif activates miR-1000 transcription and miR-1000 directly targets Myd88 in this key immune tissue. This dual function of Dif - concurrently inducing immune effectors (e.g., Drosomycin) and their suppressor miR-1000 - establishes a self-limiting circuit: Dif/miR-1000/Myd88 axis. Crucially, miR-1000-mediated suppression of Myd88, the hub of Toll pathway, constrains signal transduction and enables timely termination. Disruption of this axis prolongs Toll pathway activation and compromises host fitness during infection. Furthermore, this miRNA-adaptor regulatory paradigm is evolutionarily conserved, as miRNAs targeting MyD88 (such as miR-155) also inhibit TLR signaling in mammals. Our work reveals a transcriptionally connected feedback mechanism that dynamically restores animal innate immune homeostasis by targeting a central signaling adaptor.

v6.resumo: Em Drosophila, Dif (NF-κB) ativa miR-1000 após infecção por bactéria Gram-positiva, e miR-1000 degrada o mRNA de Myd88, fechando uma alça que encerra a sinalização Toll; no corpo gorduroso, romper o eixo prolonga a ativação de Toll e reduz a aptidão do hospedeiro na infecção.

articles.titulo: Metabolic and Signaling Pathways of Macrophage Reprogramming in Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Infarction
articles.autores: Ding Z, Wang Y, … Yu L (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction remain the predominant contributors to mortality despite advances in interventional cardiology. Chronic inflammatory responses mediated by macrophages serve as a critical determinant of the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases. This review systematically dissects the immunometabolic and signaling networks underlying macrophage reprogramming, with a focus on key cardiovascular diseases. We assess the characteristics of M1 macrophages, which involve aerobic glycolysis, activation of the pentose phosphate pathway, and disruption of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, compared to M2 macrophages that rely on oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid oxidation. Integrated signaling pathways dynamically regulate these metabolic programmes-centred on TLR/NF-κB-mediated inflammatory priming, JAK/STAT-dependent transcriptional polarization, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-AMPK-PPARγ metabolic checkpoints, which interpret microenvironmental signals to control macrophage polarization. Within atherosclerotic lesions, we demonstrate that M1-dominant macrophage populations exacerbate plaque inflammation and compromise structural integrity, whereas M2 macrophages augment inflammatory resolution and tissue restoration. Following myocardial infarction, the timely therapeutic reprogramming from M1 to M2 phenotype is essential for efficiently attenuating adverse cardiac remodeling and improving cardiac function. Targeting metabolic enzymes and signaling pathways offers a promising strategy for reprogramming macrophages and mitigating cardiovascular diseases.

articles.titulo: Drosophila CerS homeodomain sites differentially alter insulin resistance
articles.autores: Vera-Granda C, Sociale M, … Bauer R (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Ceramides are central sphingolipid intermediates whose abundance and molecular composition are closely linked to insulin resistance. Ceramide synthases (CerSs) generate ceramides and, in several family members, also contain a conserved homeodomain with poorly understood metabolic functions. Drosophila has a single CerS, Schlank, which contains a catalytic Lag1p motif and two predicted nuclear localization sequences, NLS1 and NLS2. We investigated how distinct Schlank homeodomain mutations affect high-sugar diet (HSD)-induced insulin resistance.
Endogenous KINLS1 and KIE118A knock-in alleles retained DNA binding and transcriptional repression under basal conditions but increased susceptibility to HSD-induced metabolic dysfunction. Both mutants developed enhanced hyperglycemia and impaired insulin-responsive tGPH recruitment, while KIE118A additionally showed increased FoxO nuclear localization and DILP2 retention in insulin-producing cells. By contrast, fat-body-specific switching to the DNA-binding-deficient NLS2 variant or the catalytically inactive H215D variant attenuated selected HSD-induced phenotypes, including FoxO nuclear accumulation and DILP2 retention, without fully correcting hyperglycemia or reduced body weight. Lipidomic analysis revealed extensive diet-dependent sphingolipid remodeling. In particular, NLS2 and H215D markedly reduced the fat-body ceramide pool, including abundant d14:1/20:0- and d14:1/22:0-containing Cer, CerPE, and HexCer species.
The Schlank homeodomain regulates insulin homeostasis in a site- and tissue-dependent manner. Distinct homeodomain mutations can either increase susceptibility to or partially attenuate HSD-induced insulin resistance, potentially involving insulin signaling, inter-organ communication, and sphingolipid composition.

v6.resumo: Alelos knock-in no homeodomínio da ceramida sintase Schlank aumentam ou atenuam a resistência à insulina induzida por dieta rica em açúcar conforme o sítio e o tecido: KIE118A e KINLS1 pioram hiperglicemia e recrutamento de tGPH, KIE118A acumula mais FoxO nuclear e retém DILP2 nas células produtoras de insulina, e no corpo gorduroso NLS2 e H215D reduzem o pool de ceramidas.
v6.metodo: Knock-in endógeno em Drosophila, dieta rica em açúcar, marcadores de sinalização de insulina (tGPH, FoxO, DILP2) e lipidômica de corpo gorduroso.

articles.titulo: Robust CD8 T-cell response generated via attenuated Plasmodium sporozoite prime and multi-epitope mRNA vaccine boost
articles.autores: Arumugam S, Hassert M, … Harty JT (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Plasmodium infections and subsequent malaria disease remain a global health scourge. Liver-resident and circulating memory CD8 T cells elicited by whole parasite vaccines such as genetically or radiation-attenuated sporozoites can provide potent immunity to Plasmodium infection and prevent the development of the symptomatic blood stage of infection in humans, nonhuman primates, and mice. However, this requires multiple, large doses of attenuated sporozoites, posing numerous logistical challenges. To partially address these logistical challenges, here, we prime CB6F1 mice with a human weight-normalized, subprotective single dose of genetically or radiation-attenuated Plasmodium berghei sporozoites to elicit liver-resident and circulating memory T cells prior to boosting with a novel lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccine encoding multiple CD8 T-cell epitopes from liver-stage proteins. We show that boosting primed mice with this mRNA vaccine engenders sterilizing immunity against sporozoite challenge by generating a robust liver-stage-specific CD8 T-cell response when administered intravascularly or intramuscularly. Thus, combining a single, dose-sparing attenuated sporozoite immunization with a multi-epitope translationally relevant mRNA vaccine can engender protective immunity against P. berghei sporozoite challenge via the generation of a potent circulating and resident memory liver CD8 T-cell response. Minimizing the number of attenuated sporozoite doses required to prime CD8 T cells with a full complement of liver-stage malaria-specific epitopes effectively mitigates some logistical challenges associated with attenuated sporozoite vaccination.

articles.titulo: Basophil FcεR1γ signaling regulates gut barrier integrity and systemic antibacterial immunity during malaria with a sex bias
articles.autores: Céspedes N, Fellows AM, … Luckhart S (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria predisposes individuals to concurrent bacteremia, a complication associated with increased intestinal permeability and mast cell (MC) activation. These effects correlate with elevated type-2 cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-3, IL-4, and IL-10. We previously demonstrated that basophils regulate MC activation and protect intestinal barrier integrity during malaria. Because FcεR1γ signaling is required for basophil IL-4 production, we monitored parasitemia, barrier integrity, bacteremia, and cytokine and chemokine profiles in male and female mice with basophil-specific deletion of FcεR1γ [baso Fcer1g (-)], generated by crossing Mcpt8-Cre and Fcer1gflox/flox mice. Baso Fcer1g (-) mice retain IL-3 responsiveness but fail to produce IL-4 upon activation. Mice were infected with Plasmodium yoelii 17XNL to assess the role of basophil FcεR1γ signaling during infection. Basophil FcεR1γ deficiency had no effect on parasitemia. However, female baso Fcer1g (-) mice exhibited significantly increased intestinal permeability by day 6 post-infection (PI) compared to genotype controls. Despite this enhanced barrier disruption, bacterial 16S levels in blood were reduced in female baso Fcer1g (-) mice by day 10 PI relative to female controls and mutant males. Increased permeability was associated with elevated ileal IL-6 and CCL4, and increased plasma CCL3 and CCL5 at day 6 PI. At day 10 PI, reduced bacteremia correlated with increased systemic IL-17A and GM-CSF, and reduced IL-10 and Mcpt1, indicating reduced MC activation. These findings demonstrate that basophil FcεR1γ signaling shapes female-biased mucosal and systemic immune responses during malaria, extending our understanding of sex-specific gut-systemic immune crosstalk during infection.

v6.resumo: Camundongos com deleção de FcεR1γ em basófilos, infectados com a cepa 17XNL de Plasmodium, não mudam a parasitemia, mas as fêmeas têm mais permeabilidade intestinal no dia 6, menos bacteremia no dia 10, mais IL-6 e CCL4 no íleo e mais CCL3 e CCL5 no plasma.

articles.titulo: Synergistic mechanistic and deep learning approaches for modeling insect thermal responses and geographic distributions
articles.autores: Vanalli C, van Tiel N, … Tuia D (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aim The Hutchinsonian shortfall, the lack of knowledge about species' abiotic tolerance, limits our understanding of species responses to environmental change and consequently also the outlining of their distribution in space and time. Such environmental tolerance is commonly inferred with two distinct approaches: i) trait performance studies, which use lab experiments to model species' functional responses, often overlooking real-world complexity, and ii) species distribution models, which infer environmental suitability from occurrence data, but offer limited causal insights. In this paper, we argue that these two strategies bring complementary information that can be integrated to estimate species-environment relationships more robustly and accurately map species distributions. Location Global scale Time period 2000-2019 Major taxa studied Given their exceptional diversity and climatic sensitivity, insects provide a powerful system for studying these responses. We selected key insect species representing i) disease vectors: the yellow fever (Aedes aegypti) and Asian tiger (Aedes albopictus) mosquitoes; ii) agricultural pests: the cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) and the fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda); and iii) biocontrol agents: the green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) and the 14-spotted ladybug (Propylea quatuordecimpunctata). Methods We compared predicted insect thermal suitability and distributions derived from two complementary methodological approaches: mechanistic models based on experimentally derived thermal responses of ecological rates, and deep learning-based species distribution models based on occurrence data. We further tested hybrid frameworks integrating mechanistic and correlational information through model ensembling, mechanistic regularization, and mechanistically informed deep learning. We assessed the efficacy of these methods under increasing data scarcity by progressively removing up to 80% of species occurrence records using three strategies: removal from the warmest or coldest parts of species' thermal ranges, removal from the least-sampled locations based on geographic sampling bias, and random removal as a baseline. Results Our findings highlight that occurrence-derived thermal suitability closely reproduces the observed distributions of insects. Compared to the mechanistic estimates, these thermal response curves are consistently shifted towards lower temperatures, potentially reflecting niche underfilling. However, when challenged with progressive data removal, correlative methods fail to extrapolate reliably in data-deficient regimes, where mechanistic knowledge becomes increasingly more crucial. Hybrid approaches in turn leveraged complementary information, improving predictive performance and reducing the sensitivity of environmental suitability estimates to sampling biases. Main conclusions Ultimately, we show how the synergistic integration of experimental ecology with observational biogeography can lead to more accurate and ecologically robust predictions for species distributions and their environmental responses to climatic changes.

articles.titulo: Modelling modified insect release interventions for malaria control: a scoping review and thematic comparison with dengue
articles.autores: Lakshminarayanan P, Tiley K, … Brady O (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Wolbachia is a promising new intervention for malaria control. While modelling has supported Wolbachia deployment for dengue control, its application in Anopheles is still emerging. We systematically reviewed dynamic transmission models of Wolbachia-based modified insect releases for malaria using PubMed and Embase. Evidence was compared primarily with Wolbachia-based dengue models from a parallel Wolbachia-Aedes aegypti scoping review and secondarily with gene drive-based Anopheles models identified through a separate systematic search. Across 110 included studies, three major gaps were identified. First, context-dependent fitness effects are rarely incorporated, with many models assuming high maternal transmission (MT) and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), limiting assessment of how environmental variability influences persistence. Second, spatial heterogeneity is infrequently modelled despite evidence that mosquito movement shapes Wolbachia spread. Third, few studies embed Wolbachia dynamics within integrated malaria transmission models, preventing estimation of epidemiological impact to assess Wolbachia's role in malaria control and elimination. Lessons from Wolbachia-based dengue control and parallel developments in gene drive provide an established framework, with actionable pathways for advancement. Addressing these priorities will be essential to guide safe, effective and scalable implementation of Wolbachia as a new malaria control intervention.

v6.resumo: Revisão de escopo de 110 estudos de modelos de liberação de insetos modificados (Wolbachia) para malária, comparados a modelos de dengue em Aedes aegypti e a modelos de gene drive em Anopheles; entre as lacunas, efeitos de aptidão dependentes de contexto raramente entram (muitos assumem alta transmissão materna e incompatibilidade citoplasmática) e a heterogeneidade espacial é pouco modelada.

articles.titulo: Exploring the nexus of climate-socioeconomic drivers of dengue transmission: a covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI mechanistic model
articles.autores: Adeniji A, Miller J, … He Z (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: A deterministic covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI model is developed and used to gain insight into the nexus between climate and socioeconomic parameters and the transmission dynamics of dengue. The model developed a framework that incorporates two external influences: climate and socioeconomic factors. The model is rigorously analyzed, with disease-free and endemic equilibria investigated, and is simulated using data relevant to Medellín, Colombia. We then employ machine learning algorithms as an empirical feature-selection step to identify and rank socioeconomic predictors of dengue incidence, revealing that the unemployed population is the dominant socioeconomic driver. This finding motivates the selection of unemployment as the socioeconomic covariate in the mechanistic model. From our numerical simulation, we computed using temperature only and combined [temperature + socioeconomic (unemployment)] parameters to determine how their influences drive the epidemic spread. Our model suggests that socioeconomic influence can act as a driver alongside temperature, increasing the transmission rate and leading to an earlier peak. The framework is appropriate for endemic settings where socioeconomic and climatic factors are the primary drivers of transmission dynamics. The approach demonstrates how empirical machine-learning insights can inform covariate selection in mechanistic epidemiological models, thereby strengthening interpretation of how socioeconomic and climatic conditions interact to shape epidemic potential.

articles.titulo: Fixation Matters: Multidimensional Effects of Chemical Preparation on Morphology and SEM Image Texture Features of Extremophilic Bacteria
articles.autores: Galván FS, Albarracín VH (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is widely used to investigate bacterial morphology and surface-associated features; however, sample preparation protocols may introduce artifacts that influence the interpretation of morphometric measurements and image characteristics observed in SEM micrographs. This issue is particularly relevant for extremophilic microorganisms, whose specialized cell envelopes may respond differently to chemical fixation. In this study, we evaluated two aldehyde-based fixation protocols (2.5% glutaraldehyde and Karnovsky's solution), each tested at three fixation times (1, 3, and 24 h) and with or without osmium tetroxide (OsO4) postfixation, in three Gram-positive bacterial strains: the polyextremophiles Exiguobacterium sp. S17 and Nesterenkonia sp. Act20 and the mesophile Kocuria rosea CH-021. Morphometric responses were assessed using cell surface area and surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), together with SEM image-texture analysis using Haralick-based features. Fixation conditions produced significant strain-dependent differences in both morphometric and image-texture outcomes. The magnitude of morphometric variability differed among strains, and SEM image-texture patterns were not always paralleled by morphometric measurements. These findings indicate that bacterial responses to fixation conditions are strain-dependent and support the combined use of cellular geometry and SEM image-texture descriptors for quantitative comparison of preparation conditions within a standardized SEM workflow.

articles.titulo: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
articles.autores: Tan L, Guo Z, … Li R (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS), we profile full-length RNA species of Eilat virus (EILV), a mosquito-restricted alphavirus. We found that EILV produces abundant deletion-type DVGs far exceeding those seen in related arboviruses under identical conditions. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

v6.implicacao: Imunidade & Memória Imune (priming epigenético): o sequenciamento direto lê RNA nativo de comprimento total e, em princípio, também modificações de base; conferir no texto se há análise de m6A, tema do mini-review sobre histonas e priming (o abstract não menciona modificação de base).
v6.resumo: Com sequenciamento direto de RNA em nanoporo, o Eilat virus (alfavírus restrito a mosquito) produz genomas virais defeituosos por deleção em quantidade muito maior que arbovírus relacionados nas mesmas condições; a terminação prematura na síntese do RNA genômico sugere baixa processividade da replicase, e um subconjunto de DVGs é replicado, empacotado e interfere no vírus parental ao longo de passagens seriadas.

articles.titulo: Targeting the Lactate-Lactylation Axis in Cancer Immunotherapy Resistance: From Tumor Acidosis to Context-Dependent Immune Reprogramming
articles.autores: Liang X, Lin M, … Li Y (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Lactate is now recognized as an active immunometabolic regulator in the tumor microenvironment (TME), not simply as a glycolytic byproduct. Its immunological effects arise through several related but distinct routes. Extracellular acidosis, glucose competition, and impaired monocarboxylate transporter-dependent flux can impair CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Lactate- and proton-sensing receptors can also favor suppressive myeloid and regulatory-cell programs. Histone and non-histone lactylation add another layer by linking lactate availability to chromatin regulation and protein function. During sustained or repeated metabolic stress, these processes may support regulatory T-cell fitness, suppressive programs in tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, checkpoint expression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Lactylation is a plausible mediator through which sustained metabolic stress may be converted into persistent immune reprogramming; however, post-withdrawal persistence and cellular memory remain to be demonstrated in cancer. We distinguish lactate-dependent regulation from acidosis and evaluate the links to immune dysfunction and treatment resistance by their temporal, causal, and clinical support. This framework defines tests of post-exposure persistence and connects mechanistic evidence and pharmacological specificity to biomarker development and mechanism-matched trial design.

articles.titulo: Fitness costs and effects on the peritrophic matrix associated with chitin synthase 2 gene knockout in Vip3Aa-resistant Helicoverpa zea
articles.autores: Heu CC, Schutze IX, … Fabrick JA (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Genetically engineered crops producing insecticidal Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) proteins are used globally to manage key insect pests, including Helicoverpa zea (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). In the United States, H. zea has evolved practical resistance to Bt corn and cotton producing crystalline Bt proteins and early warning of resistance to the vegetative insecticidal protein Vip3Aa has been reported. CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing that introduced disruptive mutations in the H. zea chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene facilitated creation of a strain (CHS2-KO) with 29 000-fold resistance to Vip3Aa relative to its parental susceptible strain, LAB-S. However, quantitative information about fitness costs associated with CHS2-mediated resistance remains limited. Here, we tested whether CHS2-KO exhibited costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass on diet without Vip3Aa, and examined direct effects on the peritrophic matrix (PM).
Relative to LAB-S, fitness costs in CHS2-KO were 27.8% for neonate to adult survival, 23.2% for neonate to adult development time, and 17.8% for pupal mass. An intact PM was evident in LAB-S and F1 larvae, but not in CHS2-KO larvae.
Mutations disrupting the CHS2 gene in the CHS2-KO strain of H. zea were associated with large fitness costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass when reared on diet under laboratory conditions. Also, no intact PM was evident in CHS2-KO. These results suggest that costs could oppose the spread of knockout alleles in the absence of Vip3Aa, although their magnitude on host plants and applicability to less disruptive CHS2 resistance alleles remain to be determined. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry. articles.titulo: Evolutionary repurposing of a pore-forming toxin drives epithelial remodeling during terrestrial adaptation
articles.autores: Siciliani D, Benedicenti O, … Salinas I (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The ability of vertebrates to conquer land is attributed to innovations in respiration and locomotion. However, land adaptation profoundly reshaped mucosal surfaces such as the skin, the main interface between hosts and the environment. To adapt to land, African lungfish annually remodel their skin, forming a cocoon. Here, we report the discovery of a small pore-forming toxin in African lungfish, Protop-CrTX-A, with no other vertebrate counterpart that is sufficient to drive epithelial morphogenesis transcriptional programs. In free-swimming lungfish, goblet cells secrete Protop-CrTX-A into the mucus. During estivation, this niche is replaced by a mucin-low/basal epithelial niche, adjacent to a granulocyte immune niche that becomes the predominant source of Protop-CrTX-A in the estivated skin. Protop-CrTX-A acts as a reversible switch for skin remodeling, sufficient to convert African lungfish skin between aquatic and terrestrial states. We propose that innate immunity, through its capacity to remodel tissues, was a key driver of vertebrate water-land transitions.

v6.resumo: Uma toxina pequena formadora de poro do pulmonado africano (Protop-CrTX-A) é suficiente para ativar programas transcricionais de morfogênese epitelial e funciona como interruptor reversível da remodelação da pele entre os estados aquático e terrestre; goblet cells a secretam no muco e, na estivação, granulócitos tornam-se a fonte principal. Os autores propõem que a imunidade inata, por remodelar tecidos, foi motor da transição água-terra.

articles.titulo: Shifting climates, shifting microbes: environmental determinants of the microbiome and impact on malaria transmission
articles.autores: Archaga O, Simões ML (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria transmission dynamics are governed by complex tripartite interactions between the Anopheles mosquito, the Plasmodium parasite, and the vector's gut microbiota, all mediated by the mosquito's innate immune system. Although global malaria control is increasingly hindered by drug and insecticide resistance, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding how climate shifts and environmental variations impact vector competence. While most experimental research relies on static laboratory conditions (typically fixed at 27 °C and 75-80% relative humidity), mosquitoes in nature experience continuous diurnal and seasonal environmental fluctuations that alter their physiology, immune responses, and microbiome. Here, we focus on how these environmental shifts likely influence the efficacy and translational success of innovative, microbial-based control strategies, including paratransgenesis, Wolbachia-based interventions, and microbial larvicides. By examining how climate-driven variations impact both the mosquito-microbiota-parasite system and the performance of biocontrol tools, we bridge ecological and molecular perspectives to identify the current understanding of how shifting environments influence the mosquito microbiome and microbial-based tools. We highlight the critical need to integrate dynamic climatic regimes into upstream laboratory evaluations to ensure future malaria control tools remain resilient in a global changing climate.

articles.titulo: Rapid spread of nutritional Wolbachia symbionts across and within solitary bee species
articles.autores: Preuß L, Tischer M, … Gerth M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Maternally inherited, intracellular bacteria of the genus Wolbachia are extremely widespread among arthropods. Their evolutionary success is owed to frequent host shifts and rapid subsequent spread within host populations, often facilitated by Wolbachia-induced reproductive manipulations. Theory suggests that often, Wolbachia spread may also be explained by fitness benefits, the nature of which have remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that Wolbachia's success in many solitary bee species is strongly associated with the presence of a gene cassette enabling Wolbachia to synthesize biotin (vitamin B7). This ability is absent from almost all other Wolbachia strains but common among bee-associated strains. We show that Wolbachia occurs in up to 60% of all bee species and that strains carrying this rare genomic element have independently spread into numerous bee hosts recently. We further demonstrate that the presence of the biotin operon is associated with specialized diets in several bee species, suggesting a previously overlooked nutritional role of Wolbachia in this group of important pollinators. Overall, our results suggest that nutritional benefits provided by symbionts may represent a more widespread and important mechanism by which reproductive manipulators spread into new host species than previously appreciated.

articles.titulo: Evolution: A mobile microbial toolkit for arthropod nutrition
articles.autores: Duron O (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Arthropods often overcome nutritional constraints by relying on microorganisms to provide essential metabolic functions. A recent study reveals that a mobile biotin synthesis operon provides Wolbachia symbionts with a key function that may facilitate the nutrition of solitary bees.

articles.titulo: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.autores: Amato C, Graham R, … Wood W (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

articles.titulo: Antimicrobial peptides that cross the blood-brain barrier: systematisation of data on known representatives and prospects for their use in CNS diseases
articles.autores: Martynov DD, Shamova OV (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The limited permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is one of the key obstacles in the development of new drugs for treating brain disorders. Most small molecules fail to reach therapeutic concentrations within the brain parenchyma; this causes systemic toxicity, low efficacy, and the development of drug resistance in pathogens and tumor cells. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent a large, heterogeneous group of substances that exhibit a wide range of therapeutic effects and often show low toxicity toward healthy cells. Their ability to cross the BBB independently makes them promising drug candidates for the treatment of infectious, inflammatory, and oncological diseases of the brain. To date, only a small number of peptides are known to combine antimicrobial properties with their ability to cross the BBB. Despite the significant potential of this group of molecules, experimental data on the transport of AMPs across the BBB remain fragmentary and are often obtained using incomparable experimental conditions; moreover, some earlier findings require re-evaluation in light of current knowledge regarding the barrier function of the BBB. This review provides the first systematic compilation of scattered data on peptides that combine antimicrobial activity with the capacity for transcytosis across the BBB. Three key groups of peptides have been identified and analyzed: 1) proline-rich insect AMPs (apidaecin 137, oncocin, and drosocin); 2) endogenous mammalian neuropeptides (substance P, neuropeptide Y, vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), and pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP)); 3) cell-penetrating peptides with AMP properties (penetratin, transportan 10, pVEC). The combination of antimicrobial activity and the ability to cross BBB appears to be an achievable and reproducible characteristic for peptides of various origins, thus underlying the clear need for their discovery and development.

articles.titulo: Epidemiology and Associated Risk Factors of Malaria Infection in Loka Abaya District, Sidama Region, Ethiopia
articles.autores: Melese M, Woldesenbet A, … Birmeka M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Despite continuous efforts to manage malaria, it remains a deadly disease, particularly common in low-lying areas of Ethiopia. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence, trends, and risk factors associated with malaria infection in Loka Abaya district, Sidama region, Ethiopia.
A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out using house-to-house visits from April to June 2023. A total of 186 febrile patients were chosen using systematic random sampling. Those above the age of 18 were included in the study. Five health facilities and one primary hospital in the district provided retrospective data. A systematic questionnaire and microscopic analysis of blood films were used to gather data. The blood samples were evaluated in Hantate primary hospital. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the associated factors of malaria infection. Variables with p value less than 5% were considered statistically significant.
Of 34,613 suspected patients tested for malaria over the previous 5 years, 26.2% were positive. The lowest rate recorded at 20.3% in 2018, whereas 2020 was the highest rate at 30.1%. Among them, 47.4% and 52.6% were females and males, respectively. Age groups from 5 to 14 covered up 21.6%, adults aged over 15 take up to 57.2%, and children under age 5 were 21.2%. The infection distribution was 58.8% for Plasmodium falciparum, 38.8% for Plasmodium vivax, and 2.4% mixed infections. The highest rate of infection was recorded during September to November. Cross-sectional parasitological survey showed that 18.3% of individuals were infected. The identified risk of contracting malaria was significant for individuals who were closer to mosquito breeding sites (AOR, 13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), did not use a mosquito net while sleeping (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), did not use indoor residual spraying in the previous 12 months (AOR,13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), used a window without a screen (AOR, 2.78.3, 95% CI, 1.03-13.86, p < 0.02), used a thatched roof (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), and did not know how malaria is transmitted (AOR, 4.3, 95% CI, 2.36-22.6, p < 0.04).
The study indicated that malaria remains a health issue in the Loko Abaya district. Several factors, including low income, wall openings, proximity to mosquito breeding sites, lack of indoor residual spraying, and lack of bed net use, were important predictors of malaria.

articles.titulo: Viral Infections and Dysregulation of Neurotrophin Signaling: Potential impact in the Central Nervous System
articles.autores: Miteva MT, Protto V, … De Chiara G (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

articles.titulo: TRIM5α, TRIM56 and TRIM69 differentially regulate dengue virus 2 infection through selective NS2B3-mediated antagonism
articles.autores: Paswan RR, Martins L, … Berthoux L (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus (DENV) is a major mosquito-borne human pathogen. Understanding the mechanisms of cellular resistance to the infection is vital to develop novel therapeutic tools. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins contribute to antiviral innate immunity through direct restriction of viral replication and regulation of antiviral signaling, but current knowledge on DENV targeting by TRIM proteins remains preliminary. Previously, TRIM56 was found to inhibit DENV, whereas reports on whether TRIM69 is a DENV restriction factor are conflicting. Surprisingly, the broad-spectrum viral restriction factor TRIM5 was proposed to restrict tick-borne but not mosquito-borne flaviviruses. Here, we investigated the effects of TRIM5, TRIM56, and TRIM69 on DENV serotype 2 (DENV2) infection. Overexpression experiments showed that TRIM5 and TRIM56 restrict DENV2, whereas TRIM69 enhances it. Consistently, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function showed that knocking out TRIM5 or TRIM56 increases infection, while TRIM69 knockout decreases it. Restriction correlated with reduced viral RNA and viral protein levels in TRIM5- and TRIM56-expressing cells. Virus-free experiments showed that TRIM56 downregulates the DENV2 protease complex NS2B3 levels. Reciprocally, DENV2 NS2B3 reduced TRIM56 and TRIM69 abundance independently of protease activity. RING domain-mutated TRIM56 retained partial antiviral activity and the ability to reduce NS2B3 levels, and TRIM56-NS2B3 reciprocal downmodulation effects were not counteracted by proteasomal or lysosomal inhibition. Together, these findings establish TRIM5 as a DENV2 restriction factor, reveal TRIM69 as a positive factor in DENV2 infection, suggest that TRIM5? and TRIM56 inhibit DENV2 through distinct mechanisms, and hint at proteasome-independent TRIM56-NS2B3 reciprocal downmodulation.

articles.titulo: Loss of macrodomain catalytic activity modulates Chikungunya virus
articles.autores: Bardossy ES, Bergmann L, … Saleh MC (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Viral macrodomains are promising antiviral targets that counteract host ADP-ribosylation-mediated antiviral responses in mammals. However, their role in dual-host viruses within the mosquito vector remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the role of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) nsP3 macrodomain catalytic activity by mutating the active-site asparagine 24 (N24). N24 mutant viruses rapidly selected for compensatory second-site mutations at aspartate 31 (D31) in mammalian Vero cells, while interferon-competent human cells favored reversion at position 24 instead, suggesting adaptive responses to macrodomain functional impairment. Catalytically inactive double-mutant viruses replicated poorly in interferon-competent human cells but comparably to wild-type in mosquito cells. In Aedes mosquitoes in vivo, macrodomain mutations modulated CHIKV replication and infectivity in a mutation-specific manner: one mutant reduced them while another enhanced them. Biochemical and structural analyses confirmed that these phenotypes arise in the context of a catalytically inactive macrodomain that retains ADP-ribose binding capacity, with D31 mutations lining the substrate exit path. These findings demonstrate that macrodomain catalytic activity modulates CHIKV dissemination and transmission potential in Aedes mosquitoes, revealing fundamental differences in host-dependent evolutionary advantage for a catalytically inactive viral enzyme.

articles.titulo: Unconventional modulation of Na1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
articles.autores: Zhou X, Wang H, … Liu Z (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Nav channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from Lychas mucronatus. LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Nav1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNav1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSDII) and the extracellular loop III (ECLIII) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3-S4II loop and displaces S0/S3II helices to trap VSDII within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSDII conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSDII trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECLIII engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECLIII region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Nav channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Nav channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

articles.titulo: Online extraction and preconcentration system employing a mini-column packed with 4-(2-thiazolylazo)-resorcinol-coated CoFe2O4 nanoparticles for the determination of lead in water samples by F AAS
articles.autores: de Souza Júnior JJCL, Santos BRS, … Guimarães LB (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In this study, an online solid-phase extraction system was developed that employs a mini-column packed with 4-(2-thiazolylazo)-resorcinol (TAR)-coated CoFe2O4 nanoparticles for the preconcentration and determination of lead in water samples by flame atomic absorption spectrometry. The synthesis of CoFe2O4 nanoparticles was accomplished through a coprecipitation method in basic media, followed by a coating process with the TAR complexing reagent. The characterization of both uncoated and coated nanoparticles was performed by means of analysis of X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Multivariate methodology was employed to optimize the flow injection analysis (FIA) system. A two-level full factorial design was employed to evaluate the factors, namely eluent concentration, sampling flow rate, and pH of the sample or standard solution. The Box-Behnken design was utilized to ascertain the optimal conditions for the online system. The eluent concentration was determined to be 0.10 mol L-1, the sampling flow rate was set to 2.5 mL min-1, and the pH was adjusted to 5.0. For a sample volume of 25.0 mL and under the established optimum conditions, the online system has been shown to achieve a limit of detection and quantification of 0.9 and 2.9 μg L-1, respectively, with an enrichment factor of 71 and a frequency of 5.7 h-1 for the determination of lead in water. The precision of the proposed method, evaluated as relative standard deviation (RSD%), yielded values of 7.3% and 6.9% for standard solutions containing 10.0 and 50.0 μg L-1 of Pb, respectively, while intraday and interday RSD values remained below 5.3% and 8.1%. The accuracy of the method was confirmed through analysis of the certified reference materials European Ultrapure Laboratory water (EUL, CRM) and European Primary Laboratory water (EPL, CRM), with an agreement ranging from 90% to 102%. The proposed flow injection analysis line system was subsequently employed for the analysis of mineral water and tap water. To evaluate the method's accuracy, an additional recovery test was also performed. The recovery values obtained ranged from 94 to 103%.

articles.titulo: A "ready to move in" osteoporosis bone regeneration material
articles.autores: Deng S, Zhao C, … Li D (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The repair of osteoporotic bone defects remains challenging because of the hostile pathological microenvironment-resembling "barren soil"-characterized by excessive oxidative stress and persistent inflammation, which impair cell survival and tissue regeneration. To address this problem, we developed a "fertile soil" implant system as a ready-to-use platform for osteoporotic bone regeneration. It consists of: (1) a three-dimensional (3D) -printed β-tricalcium phosphate/gelatin methacryloyl (β-TCP/GelMA) composite scaffold as a structural "soil matrix," and (2) a Kaempferol-loaded ZIF-8 metal organic framework as an "intelligent nutrient bank" that responsively releases zinc ions and Kaempferol in acidic osteoporotic conditions.In vitro, the implant promoted a shift in macrophage polarisation from a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype towards a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Mechanistic studies showed that this immunomodulatory effect was associated with improved mitochondrial function and reduced mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) accumulation, accompanied by suppression of the cGAS-STING-TBK1-NF-κB signaling pathway. The implant reversed inflammation-induced metabolic reprogramming in macrophages by reducing glycolytic activity and restoring oxidative phosphorylation, thereby favouring the re-establishment of immune homeostasis. In parallel, the implant directly enhanced the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and inhibited osteoclastogenesis, helping to restore the balance of bone remodelling. Conditioned-medium experiments further demonstrated that scaffold-mediated macrophage reprogramming established a pro-regenerative microenvironment that indirectly promoted osteogenesis and restrained osteoclast formation. In osteoporotic bone defect models, implantation enhanced new bone formation, improved trabecular microarchitecture, tissue integration, and vascularisation, and reduced local inflammation.In summary, this "ready-to-move in" osteoporotic bone repair system remodels the hostile microenvironment through immunomodulation and direct cell regulation, providing a "fertile soil" that may enhance bone defect repair under osteoporotic conditions.

articles.titulo: Lymphatic filariasis-associated lymphedema: pathogenesis, diagnosis, management, and global elimination
articles.autores: Narahari SR, Rajkumar P, … Murugaiyan J (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: SUMMARYFilarial lymphedema (FL), a chronic consequence of lymphatic filariasis, represents one of the most neglected manifestations of helminth infection, despite affecting an estimated 120 million individuals across tropical and subtropical regions. More than 40 million people live with irreversible limb or genital disfigurement, accompanied by lifelong pain, disability, psychological distress, and social stigma. Unlike other causes of lymphedema, FL arises from sustained host-parasite interactions, in which prolonged immune modulation, microbial persistence, and secondary infections drive progressive lymphatic damage. Disease transmission and early pathology often remain clinically silent for years, allowing lymphatic injury to accumulate before overt swelling becomes apparent. Although global elimination efforts have reduced transmission, individuals with established FL remain largely neglected, highlighting a critical disconnect between parasite control and morbidity management. Current interventions are limited to hygiene-based care, infection control, and conservative limb management; no vaccine or curative therapy exists for established lymphatic failure. Diagnostic approaches primarily capture infection status rather than ongoing immune-mediated tissue damage, constraining disease staging, monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation in resource-limited settings. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the immunopathogenesis of FL, emphasizing the roles of chronic inflammation, genetics, immune dysregulation, microbial translocation, and lymphatic adipose tissue remodeling in disease persistence. We highlight emerging diagnostic biomarkers, therapeutic targets, and integrative management strategies, and outline critical gaps that hinder effective morbidity reduction. Advancing stage-specific diagnostic approaches and exploring intervention mechanisms will be essential to improve quality of life for affected individuals and achieve meaningful, sustainable elimination of lymphatic filariasis-associated morbidity.

articles.titulo: T/NK-cell remodeling and IFN-responsive myeloid activation delineate immunometabolic risk profiles in chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease
articles.autores: Cao Y, Zhou Z, … Zhang W (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus disease (CAEBV) is a rare EBV-associated T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by persistent viral infection, systemic inflammation, and highly variable clinical courses. Patients may develop HLH-like hyperinflammation, severe organ involvement, lymphoma transformation, or death, yet current assessment does not fully explain why patients with similar viral burden follow divergent trajectories.
We integrated PBMC single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from healthy controls and CAEBV samples with a retrospective cohort of 130 independent CAEBV patients to connect cellular immune remodeling with clinically measurable features.
Single-cell analysis identified T/NK remodeling toward cytotoxic, exhaustion-associated, senescence-associated, and metabolically altered states, accompanied by IFN-responsive, antigen-presenting myeloid programs. Ligand-receptor and receiver-side analyses prioritized candidate IFNγ-associated T/NK-to-myeloid communication within this IFN-responsive program, linking NK and CD8+ T-cell states with myeloid inflammatory activation. Guided by these findings, we mapped inflammatory, metabolic, coagulation, and lymphocyte-subset variables into a biology-informed clinical immunometabolic index reflecting inflammatory cytokine activation, metabolic stress, and adaptive immune contraction. Internally defined index strata were associated with increasing CAEBV+HLH, death, and severe-disease burden. Unsupervised clinical mapping further identified three exploratory but interpretable immunometabolic patterns, including immune-metabolically preserved, intermediate immune-contraction, and IFNγ-high immunometabolic high-risk, with distinct immune-cell, inflammatory, metabolic, and outcome profiles.
Together, these findings organize CAEBV heterogeneity around linked T/NK remodeling, myeloid activation, and systemic immunometabolic stress. This single-cell-informed clinical-pattern map complements EBV-DNA and organ-size assessment and supports prospective validation of clinically measurable, mechanism-guided monitoring and intervention strategies.

articles.titulo: Recent Developments in Sulfonamide-Based Anti-Malarial Agents: Structure-Activity Relationships and Future Perspectives
articles.autores: Kong SH, Chauhan S, … Qin HL (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Despite tremendous advancements in prevention and treatment, malaria continues to be one of the deadliest infectious illnesses in the world and a persistent public health concern. The critical need to find new chemotherapeutic drugs with better efficacy, selectivity, and resistance profiles is highlighted by the widespread rise of resistance to traditional anti-malarial drugs. Due to their exceptional structural adaptability, advantageous pharmacokinetic characteristics, and capacity to modulate several biological targets involved in the Plasmodium life cycle, sulfonamide-based compounds have garnered significant attention in anti-malarial drug discovery among the various classes of bioactive molecules. Many derivatives with strong action against drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant strains of Plasmodium falciparum have been produced via structural modifications of the sulfonamide pharmacophore. All things considered, this review offers insightful information about the medicinal chemistry of sulfonamide derivatives and a strategic framework for the logical development of novel anti-malarial treatments.

articles.titulo: Saponins and Sapogenins in Inflammation Therapeutics: Glycosylation-Dependent Mechanisms, Pharmacokinetics and Advanced Delivery Solutions
articles.autores: Qin M, Fu Y, … Gao X (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Saponins and their aglycones, the sapogenins, are the bioactive constituents of medicinal herbs such as Panax ginseng and Astragalus membranaceus, and they act on inflammation at several levels at once. The canonical nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome cascades are the best-replicated entry points, and beyond them these compounds modify non-coding RNA networks and post-translational regulation and reshape immuno-metabolic circuits by suppressing glycolytic enzymes and engaging AMPK-dependent energy sensing. Whether a given activity belongs to the glycoside or to the aglycone is often unclear, because orally administered glycosides are extensively deglycosylated by the intestinal microbiota, and this review therefore organises the evidence by glycosylation status and annotates every compound accordingly. Translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility, low and variable bioavailability, structural instability, and dose-dependent toxicity, and stimulus-responsive nanocarriers, exosome-based systems, and microbiota-aware pharmacokinetic modelling are the most credible routes past these barriers. The mechanistic picture that emerges is coherent but still provisional, and progress now depends less on further pathway catalogues than on experiments that establish direct target engagement and on pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data obtained in human-relevant models.

articles.titulo: Integrated metabolomics reveals nervonic acid-associated immunometabolic
articles.autores: Xu Y, Xu D, … Qin L (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits profound metabolic heterogeneity, yet the functional lipid metabolites driving tumor progression and immune microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to construct a metabolomic atlas of HCC and identify clinically relevant metabolic vulnerabilities.
Untargeted metabolomic profiling was performed in 91 paired HCC and adjacent non-tumor tissues. Integrated metabolomic, transcriptomic, clinicopathological, and immune analyses characterized metabolic heterogeneity. Nervonic acid was evaluated in HCC cells, immunocompetent and immunodeficient mouse models, and knockdown and rescue experiments targeting ATP citrate lyase (ACLY).
HCC showed extensive metabolic remodeling with limited metabolite-gene concordance. Clustering identified four metabolomic subtypes. The high-risk subtype MS1 exhibited poor prognosis, pronounced very-long-chain fatty acid remodeling, and immunosuppressive features. Nervonic acid, a very-long-chain monounsaturated fatty acid, was enriched in MS1, increased in HCC tissues, and associated with unfavorable survival. It promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth. In immunocompetent models, nervonic acid reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and increased M2-like macrophage enrichment. Exploratory CD8 depletion suggested attenuation of the nervonic acid-associated tumor growth increment. Coordinated lipid remodeling included altered free fatty acid composition, enhanced fatty acid uptake, increased cholesterol abundance, and changes in membrane lipid order. Nervonic acid induced an ACLY-centered lipogenic program; in HCC cells, ACLY knockdown attenuated malignant phenotypes and lipid accumulation, and ACLY rescue restored these responses.
Nervonic acid marks an aggressive HCC subtype with distinct immune features. Knockdown and rescue in HCC cells implicate ACLY in lipid remodeling. The prognostic value of tumor nervonic acid requires independent validation.

articles.titulo: Understanding Nonreacting Substrate Analogs as Potential Scaffolds for Inhibitor Design Against Mycobacterium tuberculosis Cystathionine β-Synthase
articles.autores: Polepalli S, Roy A, … Dutta S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mycobacterium tuberculosis cystathionine beta-synthase (MtbCBS), a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme, regulates sulfur metabolism and redox homeostasis, making it a model enzyme for inhibition studies and to understand scaffold behavior. Amino acids remains as an attractive scaffold for designing novel inhibitors having reduced cytotoxicity and improved properties for cellular uptake. This study integrates computational, biophysical, and structural approaches to provide for a potential scaffold that could be further modified to inhibit MtbCBS. Structure-based sequence alignment of CBS homologs identified seven conserved polar/charged regions critical for PLP-substrate interactions. Molecular docking of polar substrate analogs (threonine, histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine) at the conserved active site revealed distinct binding modes for histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated persistent binding of histidine, stabilized by hydrophobic interactions relative to other analogs. Experimental studies revealed histidine's ability to form stable external aldimine adducts, modulating enzyme thermostability (ΔTm), akin to known reacting substrates. Finally, cryo-EM-based structural studies revealed two classes of MtbCBS, one with extra density suggesting the noncovalently bound histidine and the unbound WT MtbCBS maintaining internal aldimine. This suggests that exploration of the chemical modification space of the histidine moiety might provide us with a potential inhibitor against MtbCBS and enzymes of the RTS pathway.

articles.titulo: Case report: A worm's eye view: Fatal intraocular Dirofilaria immitis in a domestic cat from Georgia, USA
articles.autores: Jones H, Yared K, … Yabsley MJ (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dirofilaria immitis (canine heartworm) is a mosquito-transmitted nematode for which the domestic cat (Felis catus) is an aberrant host. Feline infections typically involve low worm burdens, unisex or developmentally arrested specimens, absent or transient microfilaremia, and unreliable antigen serology. Ectopic larval migration to the ocular anterior chamber is rarely reported. We describe a fatal case of intraocular D. immitis in a 6-year-old male neutered indoor/outdoor domestic shorthair from Walton County, Georgia, USA. The cat presented to a local veterinary hospital with lethargy, hyporexia, and an owner-observed organism in the right eye (OD); examination revealed anterior chamber opacity, and a presumptive diagnosis of ophthalmomyiasis interna likely due to a Cuterebra species. Prior to referral, the cat received selamectin/sarolaner (Revolution® Plus), epsiprantel (Cestex), and a rabies vaccine. At the referral center, the cat developed recurrent seizure-like episodes and died overnight despite supportive care. A SNAP Feline Triple Test (IDEXX) was negative for heartworm antigen, FeLV antigen, and FIV antibody. Post-mortem enucleation of OD revealed a single nematode (10.74 cm) within the anterior chamber. The worm was morphologically consistent with Dirofilaria and was confirmed to be D. immitis by sequence analysis of the COI and 18S rDNA gene targets. This case highlights the limitations of feline heartworm testing, initial clinical misidentification, morphologic limitations in aberrant host-tissue combinations, and the importance of pre-treatment microfilaremia assessment.

articles.titulo: Endoplasmic reticulum stress promotes ferroptosis in ventilator-induced lung injury by promoting HRD1-dependent GPX4 ubiquitination via the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway
articles.autores: Jiang Y, Ling M, … Ye L (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is a serious complication of mechanical ventilation. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) has been implicated in regulating ferroptosis, and we previously linked ERS to VILI-associated inflammation. However, how ERS mechanistically drives ferroptosis during VILI remains unclear.
C57BL/6J mice were pretreated with the IRE1α RNase inhibitor STF-083010 or the HRD1 inhibitor LS102 before high tidal volume (HTV) ventilation for 4 h. Mouse lung epithelial cells were transfected with sgGpx4, siHrd1, or corresponding controls and then subjected to 20% cyclic stretch (CS) with or without ferrostatin-1. Lung injury was assessed by H&E staining, wet/dry ratio, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) protein and cell counts. Inflammation was quantified by ELISA and qRT-PCR. Ferroptosis was evaluated by transmission electron microscopy and measurement of malondialdehyde (MDA), Fe²⁺, and reactive oxygen species (ROS). Protein abundance and localization were analyzed by immunoblotting and immunohistochemistry. HRD1/GPX4 interaction and GPX4 ubiquitination were examined by co-immunoprecipitation and ubiquitination assays.
HTV ventilation induced severe lung injury with ferroptotic features and reduced SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression. STF-083010 alleviated lung injury and inflammation, suppressed ferroptosis, and restored SLC7A11/GPX4, while attenuating HRD1 upregulation. GPX4 deletion markedly increased susceptibility to CS-induced cell death and was not rescued by ferrostatin-1. Mechanistically, HRD1 interacted with GPX4 and promoted its ubiquitination and degradation under injurious ventilation. HRD1 knockdown preserved GPX4 stability and reduced CS-induced ferroptosis. Consistently, LS102 mitigated ferroptosis, lung injury, and inflammatory responses in vivo.
ERS promotes ferroptosis in VILI through an IRE1α/XBP1-HRD1 axis that drives ubiquitin-mediated GPX4 degradation. Targeting HRD1 or upstream IRE1α RNase activity preserves GPX4, limits ferroptosis, and attenuates VILI, supporting this pathway as a therapeutic target.

articles.titulo: Urolithin A mitigates behavioural and synaptic deficits associated with epilepsy
articles.autores: Mishra S, Verma V, … Nongthomba U (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The persistence of drug-resistant epilepsy highlights the need for new therapies that target novel mechanisms while maintaining synaptic strength and minimizing side effects. Small molecules of natural origin with anti-epileptogenic potential can influence altered synaptic deficits and reducing seizure threshold, offering a strategy to restore cellular energy homeostasis and slow the progression of epilepsy and associated comorbidities.
We used a combination of approaches including behavioural assays, immunostaining and electrophysiological recordings to study the synaptic contributions to reduced seizure-threshold in both Drosophila and mouse models of epilepsy. In addition, we used affinity-purification with synthesized beads specific for our small molecule to identify its cellular partners.
We found that administration of Urolithin-A (UA), a small molecule of natural origin, mitigated behavioural and synaptic dysfunctions under chemically and genetically induced epileptic conditions in Drosophila. Additionally, chronic treatment with UA attenuated the altered single-cell and network synaptic transmission in PTZ-induced chronic kindling of mice. However, UA exerted no seizure-suppressive effects in in vitro epileptic conditions, suggesting the absence of acute anti-epileptic effects. In addition, we identified the direct interactor of UA as the complex of tubulin dimer and VDAC1. Molecular docking analyses also predicted that urolithin A interacts with VDAC1. Consistent with the neuroprotective role of VDAC1 downregulation reported in previous studies, neuron-specific knockdown of VDAC1 in Drosophila phenocopied the effects of UA.
Collectively, our data show that UA exerts disease-modifying anti-epileptic effects in both Drosophila and mouse models with VDAC1 identified as a critical functional mediator; however, direct functional modulation of VDAC1 and associated partners by UA will require further experimental validation. These findings provide the blueprint for future drug discovery targeting VDAC1-dependent pathways.

articles.titulo: Targeting endoplasmic reticulum-associated glucose-6-phosphate metabolism sensitizes glioblastoma to chemoradiotherapy
articles.autores: Vitale F, Losacco S, … Marini C (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Antioxidant capacity is a major determinant of glioblastoma (GBM) resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) and radiotherapy (RT). Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) metabolism, regulated by hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) and glucose-6-phosphatase 3 (G6PC3), sustains ER-linked nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) production and thereby supports glutathione (GSH)-dependent redox buffering; however, its clinical relevance and therapeutic exploitability in GBM remain poorly defined.
Public GBM transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to assess the prognostic relevance of H6PD and G6PC3 expression. U87 GBM cells were treated with TMZ and fractionated RT, with or without transient chlorogenic acid (CGA) exposure administered prior to irradiation. CGA was selected as a modulator of ER G6P metabolism due to its capability to inhibit G6P transport across the reticular membrane. Cell survival, oxidative stress, intracellular redox balance, and metabolic activity were evaluated.
High expression of H6PD and G6PC3 predicted poorer patient survival, with H6PD retaining independent prognostic significance, identifying ER-associated G6P/NADPH metabolism as an adverse metabolic signature in GBM. Transient CGA exposure significantly potentiated TMZ + RT cytotoxicity, increasing membrane damage and reducing cell survival after irradiation. CGA induced an early increase in oxidative stress followed by delayed depletion of reduced NADPH and GSH, amplifying redox imbalance under combinedchemoradiotherapy. Metabolic analyses indicated enhanced glycolytic engagement without further stimulation of mitochondrial respiration.
ER-associated NADPH metabolism represents a clinically relevant determinant of redox resilience in GBM, with H6PD emerging as an independent prognostic marker within this metabolic axis. In a U87 proof-of-concept model, transient, timing-based metabolic priming with CGA disrupts antioxidant buffering and amplifies oxidative vulnerability during chemoradiotherapy, thereby enhancing tumor in vitro. These findings provide a strong mechanistic and translational rationale for targeting ER-linked redox metabolism as an adjuvant strategy to improve GBM responsiveness to standard chemoradiotherapy.
