articles.titulo: Validating regional insect pest phenology forecasts using published developmental data
articles.autores: San-Segundo Molina D, Stefanescu C, Morales-Castilla I (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: BACKGROUND: Crop losses caused by insect pests are expected to increase under global warming, highlighting the need for accurate phenology forecasts to support integrated pest management (IPM). Arthropod pests, as ectotherms, exhibit temperature-dependent development and phenology that can be described by thermal performance curves (TPCs). For decades, developmental models have predicted pest emergence through thermal accumulation approaches, yet it remains unclear to what extent experimentally derived development models can accurately predict field phenology across spatial and temporal scales. Here, we evaluate whether developmental TPCs and linear degree-day models fitted from published experimental data can predict large-scale pest phenology under a rate-summation approach. RESULTS: We compiled published developmental data for the widespread crucifer pest Pieris rapae and fitted several TPCs and linear degree-day models. Model predictions were validated against independent long-term monitoring data from the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme for mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. Published experimental data accurately predicted large-scale pest emergence, with prediction errors generally below one week. However, predictive performance depended strongly on the spatial and temporal scale considered, with model rankings changing according to the scale and temperature resolution used. CONCLUSION: Published experimental thermal biology data can accurately predict regional insect pest phenology when developmental models are selected according to the intended forecasting scale. These findings provide practical guidance for improving pest alert systems and other decision-support tools, while demonstrating how decades of experimental research can be translated into operational phenology forecasting.

articles.titulo: Differential modulation of host cell Serine and Arginine-Rich (SR) protein and apoptotic factor BCL-2
articles.autores: Mandal D (1 autor)
articles.resumo_original: Regulation of alternative splicing (AS) is important in controlling cellular functions. More than 95% human genes are alternatively spliced and AS is regulated by close to 100 splicing factors. Line of evidences suggest that virus infections alter the AS pattern of numerous host genes. In this study we have investigated Chandipura virus (CHPV) induced alteration of host cell SR protein gene expressions and determined if these changes have any effect on apoptotic factor BCL-2 levels. CHPV is a negative stranded RNA virus which causes fever, brain encephalitis and death among young children with a case-fatality rate of 50%. Few studies were done in past to understand the roles of host factors in CHPV pathogenesis and no study was done on virus induced changes in AS. Our study showed that there is a down-regulation of SR proteins SRp55 and SRp75 expression levels significantly decreased in the CHPV infected Vero E6 cells compared to uninfected cells. For a comparison, we also looked at the levels of SRp55 and SRp75 in dengue virus (DENV) infected cells. Our results showed that SRp75 levels is unchanged whereas SRp55 levels increased in DENV infected cells. We have also determined the levels of large and small splice variants of apoptotic gene BCL-2 to find out possible correlation between the altered splicing factor expressions and virus infected cell death via apoptosis. Our data indicates that in CHPV infected cells, BCL-2 large splice variant expressions decreased as compared to uninfected cells. This is the first study of CHPV mediated alteration of splicing factor expressions and these results warrant further study with other viruses to better understand the global changes in host splicing events, cell survival, host immune response during virus infection.

articles.titulo: A DNA barcode reference library of the mosquitoes of Iran: insights into species boundaries and evolutionary relationships
articles.autores: Norouzi B, Oshaghi MA, … Azari-Hamidian S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquitoes (Diptera: Culicidae) are the most significant arthropods in public health. In Iran, 73 species across eight genera are known to occur, including 35 species and seven genera in Guilan Province. Due to challenges in morphological identification, this study evaluated the utility of DNA barcoding for mosquito species identification in Iran. Sampling was conducted from 2022 to 2024 across five counties in Guilan Province. Species were initially identified morphologically, followed by molecular analysis using the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene. Sequences were compared with reference data in GenBank, and phylogenetic trees were constructed using the Maximum Likelihood method. A total of 13151 adult mosquitoes were collected and morphologically identified including 17 species, with COI sequences generated for 15 species, 10 of which are newly barcoded from Iran. Phylogenetic analysis of the genera and species of Aedes, Anopheles and Culex was performed. The analysis revealed a close genetic relationship between Cx. pipiens and Cx. quinquefasciatus (p-distance = 0.019); however, diagnostic nucleotide positions successfully differentiated Iranian specimens. Within the genus Anopheles, An. hyrcanus and An. pseudopictus formed closely related clades (p-distance = 0.023), underscoring the challenging debates of the Hyrcanus Group with the COI gene and the need for complementary markers. Overall, COI-based phylogeny supported the traditional classification of the genera, subgenera and species of Iranian mosquitoes. DNA barcoding clearly displayed the geographical and phylogenetic affinities of Iranian species and served as a suitable tool for tracing distributional routes, whether natural or anthropogenic.

articles.titulo: The targeted modulation of the inflammatory response to alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via a biomimetic allicin delivery platform
articles.autores: Gao Y, Yin J, … Li X (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Reperfusion strategies, the clinical standard for acute myocardial infarction, inevitably trigger severe myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury. The acute phase of MI/R causes dual imbalance: excessive cardiomyocyte apoptosis and impaired macrophage phagocytosis. This pathological mechanism, the aberrant accumulation of apoptotic cells, triggers secondary necrosis, thereby serving as a critical driver of inflammatory storm and maladaptive cardiac remodeling. However, there is currently no targeted anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategy for this early pathological mechanism. To break these treatment limitations, we engineered a biomimetic stem cell membrane-camouflaged, allicin-loaded metal-organic framework nanoplatform (MOF-Al@NVs). Leveraging the nanovesicles' ischemic homing capability and the MOF's high drug-loading capacity and acidic degradation properties, this platform enables rapid, targeted delivery and release of allicin (which has anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory effects) within the ischemic myocardium. In vitro and in vivo investigations demonstrate that MOF-Al@NVs efficiently rescue dying cardiomyocytes by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts and blocking the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Concurrently, the platform re-orchestrates cardio-immune homeostasis by cooperatively upregulating the efferocytic receptor axis (TREM2/MERTK) on macrophages via activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade. This dual coordinative effect accelerates the clearance of cellular debris and promotes the anti-inflammatory phenotypic transition from M1 to M2 macrophages, thereby attenuating the inflammatory storm, ameliorating acute-phase MI/R-induced cardiac dysfunction, and improving short-term prognosis. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics, integrated with multi-omics, confirms that MOF-Al@NVs effectively restore spatial immunometabolic homeostasis in the early infarct border zone. This biomimetic nanoplatform offers a promising strategy for targeted anti-inflammatory therapy in early MI/R injury.

articles.titulo: Cell-informed host-response profiling distinguishes neutrophil-like and PLA2G7-associated immunometabolic axes in systemic infection
articles.autores: Gu Y, Yu Y, … Ding S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Whole-blood host-response signatures can distinguish infection-positive from infection-negative systemic inflammation, but their signal combines changes in leucocyte composition with regulation within cells. We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product.
A 12-gene framework was retrospectively derived from four contrasts across three studies (444 contrast-level observations; 443 unique arrays) and subsequently fixed for external evaluation using a single-sample transcriptome-rank score. Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context.
In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764-0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on population and comparator context. Adjustment for alternative neutrophil-associated transcript scores produced a marker-dependent ordering, with SMPDL3A among the most attenuated and PLA2G7 among the least attenuated candidates; no candidate remained FDR-significant in the primary six-gene family. Donor-level single-cell analysis and qRT-PCR supported a monocyte/macrophage context for PLA2G7 and granulocyte-like localization of the diagnostic immune markers. Exploratory Mendelian randomisation did not support a susceptibility effect for the testable immunometabolism-associated candidates, and the HLA-DRB1 regional signal lacked evidence of a shared variant under single-variant colocalisation assumptions.
This study provides an auditable, cell-informed framework that relates granulocyte-associated transcription to PLA2G7-associated monocyte/macrophage localization within the whole-blood infection response. The framework is intended for biological prioritisation, and it defines testable candidates for future studies.

articles.titulo: Exploring Neem Phytochemicals as Potential Inhibitors of Trehalose-6-Phosphate Synthase
articles.autores: Bella-Omunagbe M, Adebayo AH, … Chinedu SN (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Increasing resistance to insecticides and their accompanying off-target effects call for the development of biodegradable insecticides with selective metabolism-based targets. Anopheles gambiae trehalose-6-phosphate synthase (AgTPS), the first enzyme in the trehalose metabolic pathway, is essential for key developmental processes in the organism but absent in vertebrates, making it an attractive insecticidal target. This study aims to evaluate the inhibitory potential of neem-derived compounds against AgTPS using in silico methods. The 3D structure was predicted, and its active-site residues were identified based on conserved TPS homologues. A library of 275 neem phytochemicals was compiled from IMPPAT and Dr Duke's databases, alongside known substrates and inhibitors. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock Vina at the glucose-6-phosphate (G6P), UDP-glucose (UDPG), and combined binding sites. Protein-ligand interactions were analysed using LigPlot+, while insecticide-likeness and ADMET properties were evaluated using QEPest and pkCSM. Several neem-derived compounds exhibited stronger binding affinities to AgTPS than the natural substrates across all binding sites. Tannic acid showed a high binding affinity across all binding sites, with a range of -11.3 to -12.1 kcal/mol, showing interactions with conserved catalytic residues. Other compounds, including 1-cinnamoylmelianolone, nimbilin, 6-acetylnimbandiol, and 7-deacetyl-7-oxogedunin, also demonstrated strong and consistent binding, frequently outperforming known TPS inhibitors. ADMET analysis revealed that tannic acid possessed unfavourable pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles. In contrast, limonoids such as 1-cinnamoylmelianolone and nimbilin displayed a more favourable balance between potency, insecticide-likeness, and predicted safety. Neem-derived phytochemicals show significant potential as inhibitors of AgTPS, supporting AgTPS as a promising target for selective mosquito control. While tannic acid demonstrates strong binding affinity, its poor drug-likeness limits practical application. The limonoids, such as 1-cinnamoylmelianolone and nimbilin, thus emerge as more viable lead candidates. These findings provide molecular insights into neem's insecticidal activity and support further experimental validation for vector control applications.

articles.titulo: A Male-Specific Immunometabolic Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell Transcriptomic Signature in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
articles.autores: Bura A, Noh MY, … Kim SH (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) demonstrates well-recognized sex-related differences in incidence, age at onset, and clinical features, but the biological mechanisms underlying this heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Peripheral immune mechanisms have been proposed as potential contributors.
We performed sex-stratified transcriptomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from a clinically well-characterized cohort of 60 participants: 15 male ALS participants, 15 female ALS participants, and 30 sex-matched healthy controls. Differential gene expression and pathway enrichment were analyzed, followed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) validation and correlation with clinical parameters, including plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels.
PBMCs from male ALS participants exhibited extensive transcriptional alterations, with coordinated downregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation pathways and upregulation of the extracellular matrix and inflammatory signaling. In contrast, PBMCs from female ALS participants showed minimal and less-consistent transcriptomic changes. These findings were validated by qPCR. Notably, changes in mitochondrial and immune-related transcripts were not associated with the plasma NfL level, disease progression rate, or clinical severity.
This study has identified a male-specific peripheral immunometabolic transcriptomic signature in ALS that is independent of established biomarkers of neurodegeneration. These findings may help to explain sex-related differences in disease pathogenesis and clinical presentation, and they underscore the importance of considering sex as an influential biological variable in ALS.

articles.titulo: Vitamin D3 Attenuates Experimental Colitis with PPARγ-associated regulation of macrophage lipid accumulation
articles.autores: Lu J, Hu Q, … Zhang J (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) and its active metabolite calcitriol exert immunoregulatory effects, but their macrophage metabolic actions during intestinal inflammation remain incompletely defined. We examined oral vitamin D3 in experimental colitis and explored vitamin D receptor (VDR)-associated peroxisome proliferator-activated receptorγ (PPARγ) involvement in macrophage responses to calcitriol. In a dextran sulfate sodium-induced mouse model, oral vitamin D3 reduced disease activity, colonic injury, macrophage infiltration and inflammatory cytokine production, and partly normalized selected serum lipid parameters, with dose-related increases in serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25-(OH)2D3). In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages, calcitriol lowered IL-6 and IL-12/23p40, increased IL-10 and TGF-β, reduced M1-like/M2-like macrophage ratio, and decreased intracellular triglyceride, cholesterol and lipid-droplet accumulation. Oral vitamin D3 restored colonic PPARγ expression, PPARγ knockdown attenuated the effects of calcitriol on cytokine release and lipid accumulation. Murine colon microarray data linked myeloid Pparg deficiency to higher expression of inflammatory genes and lower expression of selected lipid-metabolism genes. Human UC macrophages with detectable VDR transcripts had higher PPARγ-target and lipid-metabolism module scores. These findings support anti-colitic effects of oral vitamin D3 and suggest VDR-associated PPARγ involvement in the macrophage response to calcitriol.

articles.titulo: Draper-mediated efferocytosis by Drosophila imaginal disc epithelial cells clears cellular debris during regeneration
articles.autores: Mathure SA, Maghinang K, … Smith-Bolton R (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Regeneration is a coordinated process that restores tissue integrity following damage. Following injury, tissues initiate early responses, including epithelial remodeling and clearance of cellular debris. However, how debris clearance is coordinated with regenerative growth to ensure efficient tissue repair remains poorly understood. To address how early damage responses, particularly debris clearance, are coordinated with regeneration, we used a genetic ablation system in Drosophila wing imaginal discs to induce apoptosis in the pouch region. Targeted damage generates cellular debris that localizes to both the apical and basal sides of the epithelium. We show that most cellular debris is cleared within two days after damage, although some debris persists apical to the regenerating epithelium. Our data indicate that residual debris consists of a heterogeneous mixture of cellular components, suggesting no preferential targeting by the clearance machinery. Notably, immune cells are not recruited to the damaged tissue due to restricted access by an intact basement membrane. Instead, we discovered that debris clearance is mediated by efferocytosis, whereby neighboring hinge epithelial cells activate JNK signaling and engulf debris via lysosomal formation. Reduction of efferocytosis by mutation of the phagocytic receptor Draper delays debris removal and increases debris persistence. This impairment has a modest impact on regeneration, as measured by adult wing size. Together, our results reveal a previously unappreciated role for epithelial cells as non-professional phagocytes for debris clearance during regeneration.
